([[Blairstown, New Jersey]]) | college = * [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] (2014–2017) * [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] (2018–2019) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * [[Associated Press|AP]] Honorable Mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2019 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2019]]) * First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2019) * [[Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament|Big 12 Tournament]] MVP ([[2019 Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament|2019]]) | medaltemplates = }} '''Marial Makur Shayok''' (born July 26, 1995) is a Canadian [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]]. ==Early life== Shayok was born in Ottawa, Ontario to Sudanese father Makur and mother Hellena. Makur had some basketball talent himself — the native of Sudan played at the University of Dayton, before getting paid to play overseas. He has four siblings, including two who played college basketball in the NCAA. His sister Yar played for the University of Detroit Mercy, then signing with a pro team in France, while his older brother Shayok played at the IMG Academy and later at Bradley University.{{cite news |last1=Baines |first1=Tim |title=Marial Shayok follows family tradition after landing a scholarship to Marquette University |url=https://ottawasun.com/2013/11/08/marial-shayok-follows-family-tradition/wcm/7d9f3981-e1ba-432f-89b0-1eb685dda317 |accessdate=April 5, 2019 |work=[[Ottawa Sun]] |date=November 8, 2013}} Marial started playing basketball at the age of seven, sometimes on the playgrounds, sometimes at the YMCA, learning and honing his game alongside local legends like Greg Carter. Growing up his favourite players Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant, Penny Hardaway and Dwyane Wade, all whom play the shooting guard position as he attempts to replicate them on the court.{{cite news |last1=Baines |first1=Tim |title=Marial Shayok follows family tradition after landing a scholarship to Marquette University |url=https://ottawasun.com/2013/11/08/marial-shayok-follows-family-tradition/wcm/7d9f3981-e1ba-432f-89b0-1eb685dda317 |accessdate=April 5, 2019 |work=[[Ottawa Sun]] |date=November 8, 2013}} ==High school career== Shayok attended [[Blair Academy]], where he was coached by Joe Mantegna. He was a First Team All-Prep selection by The Star-Ledger.{{cite news |title=Boys basketball: Marial Shayok of Blair Academy commits to Marquette |url=http://highschoolsports.nj.com/news/article/-8399809458166563350/boys-basketball-marial-shayok-of-blair-academy-commits-to-marquette/ |accessdate=March 4, 2019 |work=The Star-Ledger |date=October 18, 2013}} Coming out of high school, Shayok signed with [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] but never played for the team.{{cite news |last1=Peterson |first1=Randy |title=What’s this about Marial Shayok’s very lofty 50-40-90 goal? |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/randy-peterson/2019/01/23/iowa-state-basketball-marial-shayok-surpass-cyclones-expectations-virginia/2644599002/ |accessdate=March 4, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=January 23, 2019}} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], Shayok averaged 3.8 points and 1.8 rebounds per game. The following season, he averaged 4.3 points and 1.9 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Birch |first1=Tommy |title=Virginia transfer Shayok hoping to thrive in Iowa State's system next season |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/cyclone-insider/2018/01/16/virginia-transfer-shayok-hoping-thrive-iowa-states-system-next-season/1034395001/ |accessdate=March 4, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=January 16, 2018}} Shayok posted 8.9 points and 2.4 rebounds per game for the Cavaliers as a junior, shooting 44 percent from the field and 33 percent from 3-point range. He scored 23 points in Virginia’s victory in the first round of the NCAA Tournament against the [[UNC Wilmington Seahawks men's basketball|UNC Wilmington Seahawks]]. Following the season, Shayok opted to transfer and signed with [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] on April 19, 2017.{{cite news |last1=Peterson |first1=Randy |title=Iowa State hoops lands Virginia transfer Marial Shayok |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2017/04/20/iowa-state-basketball-marial-shayok-transfer-virginia/100682812/ |accessdate=March 4, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=April 19, 2017}} Shayok scored 24 points in a 77-60 win over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] on January 5, 2019.{{cite news |title=Virginia transfer Shayok flourishing for Iowa State |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/virginia-transfer-shayok-flourishing-for-iowa-state/article_b19cd368-12c8-11e9-903d-8b4b550a7017.html |accessdate=March 4, 2019 |work=The Daily Progress |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 7, 2019}} On January 7, Shayok was named Big 12 Player of the Week.{{cite news |last1=Visser |first1=Ben |title=Marial Shayok, the Big 12's leading scorer, personifies gym-rat mentality at Iowa State |url=https://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/iowa-state-cyclones/marial-shayok-iowa-state-basketball-virginia-transfer-big-12-leading-scorer-stats-20190107 |accessdate=March 4, 2019 |work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |date=January 7, 2019}} In the semifinals of the Big 12 Conference Tournament, the redshirt senior hit a pair of big 3-pointers in the final two minutes to help five-seed Iowa State topped top seed Kansas State 63-59. Shayok finished with a game-high 21 points, helping the Cyclones battle back from a five-point deficit with 2 minutes, 47 seconds remaining. None were bigger than the final two Shayok hit.{{cite news |last1=Birch |first1=Tommy |title=A look at Marial Shayok's two big shots that helped Iowa State to the Big 12 title game|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2019/03/15/iowa-state-cyclones-marial-shayok-big-12-tournament-kansas-state/3172799002/ |accessdate=March 29, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=March 15, 2019}} On March 16, 2019, in the finals of the Big 12 Conference Tournament, Shayok scored 15 points in a 78-66 win over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and was named the [[Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament|Big 12 Tournament]] MVP to add to being named First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]].{{cite news |last1=na |first1=na |title=Iowa State's Shayok All-Big 12 first-team |url=https://wcfcourier.com/sports/basketball/iowa-state-s-shayok-all-big-first-team/article_ba48236a-d0f5-5f63-bd6f-b5f2cdceb69a.html |accessdate=March 29, 2019 |work=[[Des Moines Register]] |date=March 10, 2019}} On day two of the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]], Shayok stole the show as he scored 37 points, including a three-pointer to force overtime for his team, as well as the game-winning shot in OT. He was 7-of-9 from three-point range and also had 7 rebounds. {{cite news |last1=Parsons |first1=Brian |title=Marial steals the show at the PIT |url=https://www.wavy.com/sports/local-sports/marial-shayok-steals-the-show-at-the-pit/1937751510 |accessdate=April 18, 2019 |work=[[WAVY-TV]] |date=April 18, 2019}} He was later named as part of the
